definition: Sublation: the threefold dialectical operation of (1) negating/cancelling, (2) preserving, and (3) elevating to a higher level. The German verb aufheben contains all three meanings simultaneously. Aufhebung is the fundamental motor of dialectical progress — each stage of thought is sublated into the next, so that nothing is simply lost.

contrasts.differential: Vernichtung is abstract negation that simply destroys; Aufhebung negates while preserving and elevating
Simple negation merely denies; Aufhebung is determinate negation that produces a positive result

definition: Determinateness: the specific quality or determination that makes something what it is. Omnis determinatio est negatio — every determination is a negation, because to be something determinate is to be distinguished from what one is not. Bestimmtheit is the principle of finitude: every determinate being has its limit through negation.

contrasts.differential: Bestimmtheit is definite through negation, Unbestimmtheit is the absence of determination (pure Being)
Qualität is the immediate determinateness identical with being; Bestimmtheit is the general category under which quality, quantity, and measure fall

definition: The determinative process by which something is defined through what it is not. Hegel distinguishes abstract negation (which yields empty nothing) from determinate negation (bestimmte Negation, which preserves content and produces a new, richer determination). Determinate negation is the engine of dialectical progress.

contrasts.differential: Determinate negation is productive and content-preserving; abstract negation is destructive and yields nothing
Negation defines through exclusion, affirmation through inclusion; but for Hegel every affirmation contains negation

definition: Mediation: the process by which something relates to itself through its other. Nothing in Hegel's system is purely immediate — even what appears immediate is mediated. Vermittlung is the movement through opposition back to unity, the essential structure of all dialectical development.

contrasts.differential: Vermittlung is relation through other, Unmittelbarkeit is direct givenness; but Hegel shows every immediacy is itself mediated

definition: In-itself: the implicit, potential, or undeveloped mode of being. Something an sich has a nature that has not yet been explicitly realized or made self-conscious. The acorn is the oak an sich. Often paired with für sich (for-itself) and an und für sich (in-and-for-itself) to mark stages of development.

contrasts.differential: an sich is implicit potential not yet self-conscious; für sich is the explicit self-relation that knows itself
an sich is one-sided implicit being; an und für sich is the fully developed unity of implicit and explicit

definition: For-itself: the mode of explicit self-relation and self-consciousness. Something für sich has developed its implicit nature into self-aware actuality. In consciousness, für sich means the subject's awareness of itself as distinct from the object.

contrasts.differential: für sich is self-conscious actuality, an sich is unconscious potential
für sich is self-relation without full reconciliation with otherness; an und für sich achieves this unity

definition: Consciousness: the knowing of an object as something standing over against the knowing subject. In the Phenomenology, consciousness traverses three shapes — sense-certainty (sinnliche Gewissheit), perception (Wahrnehmung), and understanding (Verstand) — before the object is revealed as the subject's own activity, transitioning to self-consciousness.

contrasts.differential: Bewusstsein is directed at external objects; Selbstbewusstsein is consciousness turned back on itself, knowing itself as both knower and known
Bewusstsein is individual and subjective; Geist is the objective, intersubjective, and historical actuality of Spirit

definition: Self-consciousness: consciousness that has become aware of itself as both subject and object. Expressed as 'I = I' — the subject knowing itself. Crucially, self-consciousness requires recognition (Anerkennung) by another self-consciousness: 'a self-consciousness exists for a self-consciousness.' This inter-subjective requirement generates the master-slave dialectic.

contrasts.differential: Bewusstsein knows objects as external; Selbstbewusstsein knows itself, but only through the other
Selbstbewusstsein is still divided between self and other; Vernunft (Reason) achieves the unity of consciousness and self-consciousness

definition: Spirit: the self-knowing actuality that develops through history, culture, and social institutions. Geist is not merely individual consciousness but the objective reality of ethical life (Sittlichkeit), law, religion, art, and philosophy. 'The Substance is essentially Subject' — Spirit is substance that has become self-conscious.

contrasts.differential: Geist is self-conscious and self-determining; Natur is external, given, and lacks self-awareness
Bewusstsein is individual; Geist is the intersubjective and institutional actuality of a people

definition: Essence: the truth of Being, the domain of reflection and ground. Essence is Being that has gone into itself — what something truly is behind its immediate appearance. The Doctrine of Essence develops through reflection (identity, difference, contradiction) to ground (Grund), and then to appearance (Erscheinung) and actuality (Wirklichkeit).

contrasts.differential: Wesen is reflective ground; Sein is unreflected immediacy
Wesen remains in opposition between inner and outer; Begriff achieves the unity of opposites in self-developing thought

definition: The Concept: the self-developing logical form that unifies universal (Allgemeinheit), particular (Besonderheit), and individual (Einzelheit). Not a mere mental abstraction but the inner pulse of all reality. The Begriff is the truth of both Being and Essence — thinking that thinks itself and thereby generates all determinations.

contrasts.differential: Begriff is speculative thought; Vorstellung is representational thinking that separates form from content
Wesen remains in reflection; Begriff achieves self-determining unity

definition: Appearance: the showing or manifestation of Essence. Erscheinung is not mere illusion (Schein) but the necessary self-manifestation of the inner in the outer. The unity of the essential and the inessential — what appears has essential content, unlike mere semblance.

contrasts.differential: Erscheinung is the manifestation; Wesen is what manifests. They are inseparable
Erscheinung has essential content; Schein is mere semblance without substantial ground

definition: Contradiction: the internal tension within a determination that drives it beyond itself. For Hegel, contradiction is not a defect in thought but the root of all movement and life. Every finite thing contains contradiction because it is both itself and its negation. Contradiction is the deeper ground beneath opposition (Gegensatz).

contrasts.differential: Widerspruch is the motor of becoming; abstract identity (A=A) is empty tautology
Gegensatz (opposition) is external difference; Widerspruch is the unity of opposites within a single determination

definition: Becoming: the unity of Being and Nothing, the first concrete category of the Logic. Pure Being and pure Nothing are the same in their complete indeterminacy, yet their vanishing into each other is Becoming — the ceaseless movement between them. Becoming is the first example of Aufhebung.

contrasts.differential: Werden is the movement between Being and Nothing; Sein is pure indeterminate immediacy
Werden passes over into Dasein (determinate being) as its result — becoming that has come to rest

definition: Determinate being: being with a specific quality, being-there. The result of Becoming — being that has acquired determinateness through negation. Etymologically 'being-there' (Da-sein), but for Hegel the 'there' means not spatial location but definiteness. Dasein has quality (Qualität) as its immediate determinateness.

contrasts.differential: Sein is pure indeterminate being; Dasein is being with specific quality and limit
Dasein is finite and limited; Fürsichsein (being-for-self) is the infinite self-relation that results from sublating Dasein's finitude

definition: Reflection: the self-relating movement of Essence. Not merely subjective thinking about something, but the objective movement by which Essence posits itself through negation of its own immediacy. Reflection unfolds through three stages: positing reflection, external reflection, and determining reflection. It is the structure underlying identity, difference, opposition, and contradiction.

contrasts.differential: Reflexion is mediated self-relation; Unmittelbarkeit is direct givenness. But in Essence, even immediacy is itself posited by reflection
In the sphere of Being, categories pass over (Übergang) into each other; in Essence, they reflect into each other (Reflexion)

definition: Ground: the unity of identity and difference, the resolved contradiction that serves as the reason or basis for existence. Essence determines itself as ground. Ground is real mediation — essence that through its non-being returns into and posits itself. In German, Grund means both 'ground/foundation' and 'reason/cause.'

contrasts.differential: Widerspruch is the unresolved tension; Grund is the resolved contradiction that serves as the basis for existence
Ursache (cause) is an external efficient cause; Grund is the immanent reason or basis

definition: Judgment: the determination of the Concept in which the subject and predicate stand as distinct yet connected moments. Hegel connects Urteil etymologically to Ur-teil (original division) — judgment divides the unity of the Concept into subject and predicate linked by the copula 'is'. Four types of judgment correspond to Being, Essence, Concept, and the Idea.

contrasts.differential: Urteil divides the Concept into subject and predicate; Schluss (syllogism) restores their unity through the middle term
Begriff is the undivided unity; Urteil is its necessary self-differentiation

definition: Syllogism: the fully posited Concept that unites universality, particularity, and individuality through mediation. Hegel declares 'everything rational is a syllogism' — the syllogism is not merely a form of reasoning but the fundamental structure of reality. Universal, particular, and individual are united through the middle term (Mitte).

contrasts.differential: Urteil separates subject and predicate; Schluss reunites them through the mediating middle term
Formal logic treats the syllogism as an empty inference rule; Hegel's Schluss is the real structure of rational actuality
